content.title: Céline Dion to perform again after years-long health-related hiatus
content.text: Megastar singer Céline Dion has announced her return to performing after a lengthy break prompted by a rare health condition.Addressing fans in a video released on social media on Monday, which was also the 58-year-old Canadian's birthday, she said her condition had improved, and she would perform a series of shows in Paris beginning in September. "This year, I'm getting the best birthday gift of my life. I'm getting the chance to see you, to perform for you once again," Dion said."I want to let you know that I'm doing great, managing my health, feeling good."The last time the My Heart Will Go On singer headlined her own performance was on March 8, 2020, before her Courage tour was cancelled due to the COVID pandemic.Dion performing on the opening night of her Courage world tour in 2019. (AFP: Alice Chiche)Dion then disclosed she had been diagnosed with stiff person syndrome (SPS) in December 2022, and was forced to cancel the remainder of her shows indefinitely."I've been diagnosed with a very rare neurological disorder called the stiff person syndrome, which affects one in a million people," she said at the time."While we're still learning about this rare condition, we now know this is what's been causing all of the spasms that I've been having."Unfortunately these spasms affect every aspect of my daily life, sometimes causing difficulties when I walk and not allowing me to use my vocal cords to sing the way I'm used to."I Am: Celine Dion depicted how SPS affected the singer in her daily life. (Supplied: Amazon MGM Studios)What is stiff person syndrome?SPS is a rare neurological disease with symptoms that include muscle spasms, muscle rigidity, chronic pain and heightened anxiety.There is no cure for SPS, but there are treatments that can help manage symptoms. In 2024, a documentary about the singer, I Am: Céline Dion, shared details of what it took for her to continue recording and performing, including taking up to 80–90 milligrams of valium a day — more than double the safe daily dosage for adults."I don't want to sound dramatic, but I could have died," said Dion, who described how muscle stiffness caused by SPS made it hard for her to breathe, sing and walk.Despite the diagnosis, she vowed she would fight her way back to the stage.A month after the documentary's release, she sang atop the Eiffel Tower for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games opening ceremony.Céline Dion performing on the Eiffel Tower during the opening ceremony of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. (Getty Images: IOC)On Monday, Dion told fans that she has continued to feel their support despite her years off stage."Even in my most difficult times, you were there for me. You've helped me in ways that I can't even describe, and I'm truly so fortunate to have your support," she said, describing that she was now "singing again, even doing a little bit of dancing".Dion is set to perform 10 shows over five weeks at the Paris La Defense Arena beginning on September 12.ABC/AFP
